<requirement name="ledger-executable" stories="python-foundation,cli-foundation">
The product is an executable named `ledger` at the application root.
</requirement>
<requirement name="relational-storage" stories="database-step">
It stores everything in a relational database through the shipped persistence library, and every command either completes in full or changes nothing.
</requirement>
<requirement name="python-sqlite-stack" stories="python-foundation,database-step">
Implement in Python 3.11 or newer over SQLite, through the shipped Python persistence library.
</requirement>
<requirement name="pytest-tests" stories="test-suite">
Tests run under pytest.
</requirement>
<requirement name="database-location" stories="db-location">
`DATABASE_URL` names the database. A value beginning `postgres://` or `postgresql://` is a PostgreSQL DSN. Any other value is a SQLite file path, optionally prefixed `sqlite://`. When `DATABASE_URL` is unset, `DATABASE_PATH` is used, then `data/app.db`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="integer-cents-storage" stories="database-step,val-amount">
Three tables. Amounts are stored as integer cents and never as floating point.
</requirement>
<requirement name="atomic-commands" stories="db-transaction,load-accounts,load-categories,load-transactions,transfer">
**Every command is one database transaction.** A command that fails for any reason leaves every table exactly as it was. A load that rejects row 11 stores none of rows 1 to 10. A transfer stores both of its rows or neither.
</requirement>
<requirement name="no-negative-balance" stories="db-balance,load-transactions">
No command leaves an account balance below zero. An account's balance is the sum of its transaction amounts. Posting, amending, deleting, transferring, and loading are all subject to this rule, checked after the command's changes and before it commits.
</requirement>
<requirement name="account-balance" stories="account-get,report-balances">
An account's balance is the sum of its transaction amounts.
</requirement>
<requirement name="code-format" stories="val-codes">
**Codes** (`account`, `category`) are 1 to 12 characters from `A-Z` and `0-9`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="text-length" stories="val-codes">
**Names and descriptions** are 1 to 40 characters. **Memos** are 0 to 60 characters. None of them contains a comma or a newline.
</requirement>
<requirement name="amount-format" stories="val-amount">
**Amounts** on input match `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`: at most two decimal places, never zero. On output an amount is written with exactly two decimal places, a leading `-` when negative, and no thousands separator: `-12.50`, `0.00`, `5000.00`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="date-format" stories="val-dates">
**Dates** are real calendar dates written `YYYY-MM-DD`. `2026-02-30` is rejected.
</requirement>
<requirement name="assign-next-transaction-id" stories="txn-post,transfer">
A posted transaction receives one more than the largest `txn_id` present, or `1` in an empty table. A transfer's outgoing row takes that id and its incoming row the next.
</requirement>
<requirement name="keep-loaded-transaction-id" stories="load-transactions">
A loaded transaction keeps the `txn_id` from its file.
</requirement>
<requirement name="csv-output" stories="cli-output">
Every successful command except `init` writes CSV to standard output: one header row, then data rows, comma-separated, no quoting, no trailing spaces, `\n` line endings. `init` writes nothing.
</requirement>
<requirement name="failure-output" stories="cli-output">
A failing command writes nothing to standard output and one diagnostic line to standard error.
</requirement>
<requirement name="init-command" stories="schema-init">
Drops all three tables if present and creates them empty. Nothing written.
</requirement>
<requirement name="count-command" stories="schema-count">
`table,rows`, then `accounts`, `categories`, `transactions` rows in that order.
</requirement>
<requirement name="load-command" stories="load-accounts,load-categories,load-transactions">
Loads `accounts`, `categories`, or `transactions` from a file whose header matches the table's columns in the order above. Writes `table,loaded` and `<table>,<rows>`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="account-add-command" stories="account-add,val-codes">
`ledger account add <code> <name>` | The new account row.
</requirement>
<requirement name="account-get-command" stories="account-get">
`ledger account get <code>` | The account row.
</requirement>
<requirement name="account-rename-command" stories="account-rename">
`ledger account rename <code> <name>` | The updated account row.
</requirement>
<requirement name="account-delete-command" stories="account-delete">
`ledger account delete <code>` | `deleted` and the code. Refused while the account has transactions.
</requirement>
<requirement name="txn-post-command" stories="txn-post">
`ledger txn post <account> <category> <amount> <date> [<memo>]` | The new transaction row.
</requirement>
<requirement name="txn-get-command" stories="txn-get">
`ledger txn get <id>` | The transaction row.
</requirement>
<requirement name="txn-amend-command" stories="txn-amend">
`ledger txn amend <id> <amount>` | The updated transaction row. Only the amount changes.
</requirement>
<requirement name="txn-delete-command" stories="txn-delete">
`ledger txn delete <id>` | `deleted` and the id.
</requirement>
<requirement name="transfer-command" stories="transfer">
`ledger transfer <from> <to> <amount> <date>` | Two transaction rows in category `TRANSFER`: `-amount` on `<from>` with memo `transfer to <to>`, then `+amount` on `<to>` with memo `transfer from <from>`. The amount is positive and the accounts differ.
</requirement>
<requirement name="report-balances" stories="report-balances">
`ledger report balances` | `account,name,transactions,balance` per account ordered by code, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<sum>`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="report-categories" stories="report-categories">
`ledger report categories` | `category,description,transactions,inflow,outflow,net` per category ordered by code, including categories with no transactions, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="report-monthly" stories="report-monthly">
`ledger report monthly` | `month,transactions,inflow,outflow,net` per `YYYY-MM` that has transactions, ascending, then `TOTAL,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="flow-definitions" stories="report-categories,report-monthly">
`inflow` is the sum of positive amounts. `outflow` is the sum of the absolute values of negative amounts, written as a positive number. `net` is `inflow - outflow`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="exit-usage-error" stories="cli-dispatch">
Usage error: unknown command, unknown table or report, wrong argument count.
</requirement>
<requirement name="exit-operational-failure" stories="db-errors">
Operational failure: database unreachable, tables missing, file unreadable.
</requirement>
<requirement name="exit-rejected" stories="account-add,val-codes,val-amount,val-dates,load-accounts,load-categories,load-transactions,txn-post,txn-amend,transfer,account-delete,db-balance">
Rejected: invalid code, name, amount, date, or file row; duplicate key; unknown account or category; account in use; any change that would leave a negative balance.
</requirement>
<requirement name="exit-not-found" stories="account-get,account-rename,account-delete,txn-get,txn-amend,txn-delete">
Not found: `account get/rename/delete` of an absent account, `txn get/amend/delete` of an absent id.
</requirement>
<requirement name="test-script" stories="test-suite">
The completed application provides a POSIX-compatible `bin/test.sh` that runs its own automated test suite from the application root and exits zero only when every test passes.
</requirement>
<requirement name="acceptance-grader" stories="terminal-grader">
`drydock uat` runs `sh sources/run.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score.
</requirement>
